_comment: Which spelling of a substance's name to SHOW, by device region. Display only — both spellings stay searchable as aliases, so search results are identical regardless of region. `base` is shown everywhere except `alternateRegions`, which shows `alternate`. Both are stated explicitly per entry, so it does not matter which spelling the database happens to carry as the canonical row.

_region_group_notes.usAdoptedNames: Regions using US adopted names (acetaminophen, epinephrine). Canada and Japan follow USAN here, unlike most of the world.
_region_group_notes.britishSpellings: Regions keeping the British oe- spellings (oestradiol, oestrogen).

names._note: Albuterol is US-only — Canada and Japan use the INN Salbutamol.
INN is estradiol (the US and most of the world); only the UK and Commonwealth keep oestradiol.
